families.family_name: OH-rich biopolymer matrix + water-processable film-forming co-binder + 1-D clay nanochannel + complexed phosphoric acid
families.family_description: This quaternary archetype targets cold-side proton transport by combining a dense hydrogen-bonded biopolymer host, a flexible film-forming co-binder, and a 1-D fibrous/tubular inorganic confinement phase that retains a hydrated acid network. A plasticised phosphoric-acid-containing phase is used instead of neat bulk acid so that the conducting fraction is less prone to crystallisation or phase breakup between 182 and 299 K.
descriptor_match: D1: The mixed biopolymer/polymer/clay network can sustain a continuous acid-rich pathway while reducing bulk-like freezing through nanoconfinement and plasticisation.
D2: OH-rich matrices and added anti-freeze co-solvent support bound-water continuity and suppress rigidification of the polar conducting phase at sub-zero temperatures.
D3: Water-processable co-binders such as PVA or PVP can lower brittleness relative to neat biopolymer hosts and preserve film integrity at low temperature.
D4: Phosphoric acid can be held in a complexed or diluted state with polyols/water rather than as a neat crystallising phase.
D5: 1-D fibrous or tubular clays provide interconnected nanometric confinement and interfacial transport regions.
D6: Biopolymer OH/NH groups, co-binder heteroatoms, clay silanols, water, and phosphate species together create a dense hydrogen-bond relay network.
D7: The clay surface and polymer matrix can retain acid/water while avoiding complete immobilisation of the proton-conducting fraction.

families.family_name: OH-rich biopolymer or cellulose-derived matrix + anti-freeze deep-eutectic/plasticised phosphate conducting phase
families.family_description: This archetype replaces a simple acid-water phase with a strongly hydrogen-bonded, anti-freeze plasticised phosphate medium embedded in an OH-rich host. The emphasis is on retaining a mobile polar liquid fraction down to the cold end without requiring a large inorganic filler fraction.
descriptor_match: D1: A deep-eutectic or polyol-complexed phosphate phase is less likely than neat acid/water to undergo disruptive freezing or segregation.
D2: Polyol-rich or choline-based anti-freeze phases maintain hydrogen-bonded fluidity at low temperature.
D3: Plasticised polysaccharide or cellulose-derivative matrices can remain less brittle than dry neat biopolymer films.
D4: The proton source is intentionally used in a buffered or complexed form rather than as neat phosphoric acid.
D5: The conducting phase is confined within the polymer free volume and inter-chain hydrogen-bond network rather than existing as bulk pools.
D6: Polyol, phosphate, and hydroxylated host groups provide contiguous donor/acceptor sites.
D7: Host–plasticiser interactions can reduce acid exudation while still allowing proton mobility.

families.family_name: Water-processable polymer matrix + 1-D tubular/fibrous clay + buffered phosphate salt/acid hybrid conducting phase
families.family_description: This family uses a synthetic but water-processable film matrix to stabilise a partially neutralised phosphate conductor inside 1-D confinement. Relative to free-acid systems, buffered phosphate speciation is intended to improve cold stability and reduce acid crystallisation risk while preserving proton-transfer connectivity.
descriptor_match: D1: Buffered phosphate species within a polymer/clay network are less susceptible to abrupt freezing than a simple free-acid pool.
D2: Residual bound water and optional polyol plasticiser can sustain a polar conducting phase to around 200 K.
D3: Flexible water-processable polymers such as PVA/PVP/PAA can avoid severe glassy embrittlement when adequately plasticised.
D4: Partial neutralisation to dihydrogen-phosphate-containing speciation directly addresses cold-stable acid form.
D5: 1-D clay structures provide nanometric confinement and interfacial percolation paths.
D6: Polymer heteroatoms, phosphate oxyanions, and bound water create a dense hopping network.
D7: Clay and polymer functional groups can retain the conducting phase while mitigating leaching.

families.family_name: High-acid aromatic heterocycle polymer control with low-temperature plasticisation
families.family_description: This is included as a control family rather than the main recommendation. It represents the classical acid-complexed aromatic basic polymer route, but modified with added low-temperature plasticiser/water to make it at least testable in the 182–299 K window.
descriptor_match: D1: Acid-complexed basic polymers can provide continuous proton pathways, though they are more established for higher-temperature operation.
D2: Added bound water or low-volatility polyol is needed to preserve a mobile polar fraction at cold side.
D3: Without plasticisation these matrices risk low-temperature rigidity, so flexibility is only partial here.
D4: Acid is present as a polymer-complexed form rather than an unconstrained bulk phase.
D5: Nanoconfinement is weaker than in clay-containing families, making this a useful benchmark rather than the lead route.
D6: Imidazole-like basic sites plus phosphate species support proton exchange.
D7: Strong acid retention is a known strength, though over-binding risk must be managed.

instances.instance_name: Chitosan + PVA + attapulgite + phosphoric acid + glycerol membrane
instances.composition_description: Representative quaternary cold-side membrane: chitosan as OH/NH-rich biopolymer matrix, poly(vinyl alcohol) as water-processable film-forming co-binder, attapulgite (palygorskite) as 1-D fibrous nanochannel filler, phosphoric acid as proton donor, and glycerol as anti-freeze plasticiser/co-solvent. A practical starting composition would be chitosan:PVA = 60:40 by polymer mass, attapulgite 5–15 wt% of total solids, H3PO4 at 0.5–1.5 mol per repeat-unit-equivalent basic/hydroxyl site, with glycerol 10–30 wt% relative to polymers.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: likely sub-mS cm^-1 to low-mS cm^-1 at room temperature, with retained but reduced conductivity under sub-zero conditions if water/activity is controlled
acid_retention: moderate to high due to chitosan protonation and attapulgite surface adsorption
operating_temp: targeted for 182–299 K with glycerol-assisted anti-freeze behaviour
mechanical_form: solution-cast flexible membrane
risk_flags: neat phosphoric acid fraction may crystallise unless sufficiently complexed by glycerol/water/polymer
excess acid may cause leaching under humid conditions

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: OH/NH-rich biopolymer matrix providing protonatable sites, bound-water retention, and hydrogen-bond connectivity.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes chitosan-family literature analogs as proton-conducting OH/NH-rich hosts suitable for acid-complexed membranes.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Water-processable film-forming co-binder that improves casting, suppresses brittleness, and contributes hydroxyl-based hydrogen bonding.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes PVA-type membrane analogs used as hydrophilic film formers and proton-transport-supporting matrices.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: 1-D fibrous clay creating nanoconfined interfacial pathways and improving acid/water retention.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 contains attapulgite/palygorskite-like fibrous clay analogs relevant to confined proton-conducting channels.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Primary proton donor forming hydrogen-bonded phosphate/polymer/plasticiser complexes.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes phosphoric-acid-containing proton-conducting systems, supporting its role as the proton source.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Anti-freeze co-solvent/plasticiser that suppresses crystallisation and preserves low-temperature polar-fluid mobility.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes glycerol/plasticiser-type analogs used to maintain flexibility and sub-zero hydrogen-bonded fluidity.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to the closest single-paper archetype in S08 represented by manual_1157b11126 or manual_1190463586, this route is new because it explicitly combines a chitosan host, a PVA co-binder, a 1-D fibrous clay, and phosphoric acid with glycerol anti-freeze plasticisation in one cold-side-focused formulation. The mechanistic value is that each component addresses a different critical descriptor: chitosan for bound-water hosting, PVA for film continuity, attapulgite for nanoconfinement, H3PO4 for proton supply, and glycerol for anti-crystallisation. Each component has its own element-level analog in the S08 pool, but the assembled combination is proposed as a new synergy rather than copied from one paper.

instances.instance_name: Cassava starch + PVP + halloysite nanotubes + phosphoric acid + ethylene glycol membrane
instances.composition_description: Cold-side quaternary/higher-order membrane using cassava starch as the OH-rich biopolymer, polyvinylpyrrolidone as flexible water-soluble co-binder, halloysite nanotubes as 1-D tubular confinement phase, phosphoric acid as proton donor, and ethylene glycol as anti-freeze co-solvent. A workable starting point is starch:PVP = 70:30 by mass, halloysite 5–20 wt% of solids, H3PO4 20–60 wt% relative to polymer phase, and ethylene glycol 10–40 wt% relative to polymer phase.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: expected to be modest at room temperature but more persistent below 273 K than neat starch/acid films
acid_retention: moderate, improved by halloysite lumen/surface interactions and PVP complexation
operating_temp: targeted for 182–299 K with glycol-suppressed freezing
mechanical_form: castable flexible membrane with reduced starch crystallinity
risk_flags: starch retrogradation may still occur if glycol loading is too low
halloysite dispersion quality strongly affects pathway continuity
acid-rich formulation may absorb too much ambient moisture

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: OH-rich polysaccharide matrix supplying bound-water sites and a dense hydrogen-bond network.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes starch-based membrane analogs that support use of plant-derived OH-rich polysaccharides as proton-conducting hosts.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Film-forming co-binder and polar complexant that helps maintain amorphous morphology and acid compatibility.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes PVP-like hydrophilic membrane analogs used to stabilise proton-conducting polar phases.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: 1-D tubular aluminosilicate providing nanoconfinement, interfacial water retention, and percolated transport assistance.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 contains halloysite/tubular clay analogs relevant to confined proton-conducting architectures.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Primary proton donor for hybrid vehicular and hopping transport.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes phosphoric-acid-based proton-conducting systems supporting this component role.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Low-freezing co-solvent/plasticiser that suppresses low-temperature rigidification of the conducting phase.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes glycol-type plasticised proton-conducting analogs that motivate anti-freeze use.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to the closest single-paper formulations implied by manual_42051140ac or manual_58ec9a6c2e, this route is new because it merges a plant-starch host, a PVP co-binder, halloysite nanotubes, and an ethylene-glycol-complexed phosphoric acid phase in one membrane. The mechanistic gain is to couple starch hydrogen-bond density with halloysite confinement and stronger low-temperature fluid retention than a simple starch/H3PO4 membrane. Each component has S08-level analog support, but the specific combination is proposed as a new cold-side-oriented formulation.

instances.instance_name: Hydroxypropyl cellulose + choline chloride/glycerol/phosphoric acid deep-eutectic-like conducting phase
instances.composition_description: A cellulose-derived host membrane containing hydroxypropyl cellulose as the flexible OH-rich matrix and a choline chloride/glycerol/phosphoric acid/water conducting phase dispersed within it. A starting formulation could use hydroxypropyl cellulose as 50–70 wt% of dry solids, with a low-volatility DES-like phase containing choline chloride:glycerol:H3PO4 in approximately 1:2:(0.5–1) molar proportions plus controlled water.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: potentially low-mS cm^-1 class near room temperature with improved retention of measurable conductivity below 253 K
acid_retention: moderate via cellulose-derivative hydrogen bonding and ionic DES-like association
operating_temp: designed for 182–299 K with anti-freeze liquid-phase persistence
mechanical_form: soft cast film or gel-film depending DES loading
risk_flags: high DES loading may weaken dimensional stability
choline chloride hygroscopicity may complicate reproducibility
water content must be tightly controlled to avoid phase separation

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Cellulose-derived flexible OH-rich host that can remain more amorphous and less brittle than native cellulose.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes cellulose-derivative hydrophilic host analogs used in proton-conducting membrane contexts.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrogen-bond-accepting ionic component that helps form a low-freezing deep-eutectic-like conducting medium.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes DES/ionic-plasticiser-type analogs that support use of choline-based hydrogen-bonded conducting phases.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Polyol hydrogen-bond donor and anti-freeze plasticiser within the DES-like phosphate phase.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes glycerol-like anti-freeze plasticisation analogs in proton-conducting media.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Proton donor incorporated into a complexed, non-neat, low-temperature conducting phase.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes phosphoric acid as a proton donor in acid-complexed conductive systems.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Controlled bound-water fraction supporting vehicular and Grotthuss-like proton transfer.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 broadly supports water-assisted proton transport in hydrophilic membrane systems.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to simpler acidified cellulose or DES-containing polymer systems in S08, this route is new because it explicitly embeds a phosphate-bearing choline chloride/glycerol anti-freeze conducting phase within hydroxypropyl cellulose for the 182–299 K window. The key mechanistic difference is that the acid is not treated as a neat free phase; it is incorporated into a hydrogen-bonded low-freezing liquid environment designed to satisfy D1, D2, and D4 together. Each component is individually literature-plausible, but the full formulation is a new combination-level proposal.

instances.instance_name: PVA + sepiolite + potassium dihydrogen phosphate + phosphoric acid + 1,3-propanediol membrane
instances.composition_description: A buffered phosphate hybrid membrane using PVA as flexible film matrix, sepiolite as 1-D fibrous confinement phase, KH2PO4/H3PO4 as partially neutralised proton-conducting acid pair, and 1,3-propanediol as anti-freeze plasticiser. A practical starting screen would use PVA as the major matrix, sepiolite 5–15 wt%, KH2PO4:H3PO4 ratios spanning 1:0.5 to 1:2 molar, and 1,3-propanediol 10–30 wt% of polymer.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: moderate proton conductivity possible near room temperature with buffered retention at sub-zero temperatures
acid_retention: high due to phosphate salt/acid association plus sepiolite adsorption
operating_temp: targeted 182–299 K with reduced risk of neat-acid crystallisation
mechanical_form: robust cast membrane
risk_flags: partial neutralisation may reduce conductivity if over-buffered
salt crystallisation risk must be checked by DSC/XRD
sepiolite dispersion and aspect ratio control are critical

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Hydrophilic flexible film matrix and hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor host.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes PVA-based proton-conducting membrane analogs.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: 1-D fibrous clay that nanoconfines the buffered phosphate phase and helps retain polar fluid.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes sepiolite/fibrous-clay analogs relevant to confined proton transport.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Buffered phosphate salt that helps maintain a cold-stable acid speciation and reduce neat-acid crystallisation tendency.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes phosphate-salt-containing protonic analogs supporting buffered phosphate speciation.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Acid partner supplying mobile protons in equilibrium with dihydrogen phosphate species.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 supports phosphoric acid as the proton donor in phosphate-based conductors.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Low-freezing plasticiser/co-solvent preserving low-temperature segmental and fluid mobility.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes glycol/diol plasticisation analogs for low-temperature proton-conducting phases.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to the closest single-paper PVA-acid or clay-acid systems in S08, this route is new because it introduces a deliberately buffered KH2PO4/H3PO4 speciation inside a sepiolite-confined PVA matrix with a cold-side diol plasticiser. The main mechanistic value is direct alignment to D4: partial neutralisation reduces dependence on a neat phosphoric acid phase that would be risky across 182–299 K. The formulation is therefore a combination-level innovation assembled from individually supported components.

instances.instance_name: Chitosan + PVA + halloysite nanotubes + phosphoric acid membrane
instances.composition_description: Quaternary-minus-plasticiser comparison membrane using chitosan as biopolymer host, PVA as co-binder, halloysite nanotubes as 1-D confinement phase, and phosphoric acid as proton source. This is an ablation-style comparator to isolate the value of the anti-freeze co-solvent in otherwise similar confined-acid membranes.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: room-temperature conductivity may be comparable to I1, but sub-zero drop-off is expected to be stronger without dedicated anti-freeze plasticiser
acid_retention: moderate to high through polymer protonation and halloysite adsorption
operating_temp: usable as a comparison route over 182–299 K, though likely weaker at the cold end
mechanical_form: cast membrane with good shape stability
risk_flags: higher risk of low-temperature rigidification than glycerol- or glycol-containing variants
free acid domains may phase-separate if halloysite loading is insufficient

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Biopolymer matrix with protonatable NH2/OH groups.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes chitosan-host proton membrane analogs.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Film-forming hydrophilic co-binder providing flexibility and interpolymer compatibility.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes PVA membrane analogs in proton-conductive contexts.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: 1-D tubular clay confinement phase for acid/water retention and channel continuity.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes halloysite-type nanoconfinement analogs.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Proton donor acid.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes phosphoric-acid proton-conducting systems.

instances.novelty_rationale: Relative to I1 and the nearest S08 quaternary archetypes, this is a close variant because it keeps the biopolymer/co-binder/1-D clay/free-acid logic but removes the explicit anti-freeze co-solvent and changes the clay to halloysite nanotubes. That makes it useful for ablation: any low-temperature advantage of glycerol or glycol in the fuller formulations can be quantified directly. It is not positioned as the strongest cold-end candidate, but as a mechanistically informative comparator with substantial element-level precedent.

instances.instance_name: Polybenzimidazole + phosphoric acid + glycerol control membrane
instances.composition_description: Control benchmark membrane using polybenzimidazole as the acid-binding aromatic basic polymer, phosphoric acid as proton donor, and glycerol as low-temperature plasticiser/humectant. This is intended as a high-acid control rather than a lead cold-side design.
expected_properties: conductivity_range: can be competitive near room temperature when sufficiently acid-doped, but may underperform clay-confined anti-freeze systems at deep sub-zero temperatures
acid_retention: high due to strong acid-base complexation
operating_temp: benchmark/control over 182–299 K, though archetype is historically stronger at elevated temperature
mechanical_form: dense acid-complexed polymer membrane
risk_flags: over-binding of phosphoric acid may limit effective proton mobility at low temperature
cold-side flexibility may still be insufficient despite glycerol
not a low-cost water-only fabrication route compared with biopolymer families

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Basic aromatic polymer host that strongly complexes phosphoric acid.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes PBI-phosphoric-acid proton-conducting membrane analogs.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Acid dopant and proton source.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes phosphoric-acid-doped aromatic polymer conductors.

element_evidence.role_in_formulation: Auxiliary plasticiser/humectant to partially improve low-temperature mobility.
element_evidence.analog_reason: S08 includes plasticised acid-polymer analogs supporting this modifier role.

instances.novelty_rationale: This instance is retained as a control baseline rather than a novel candidate. It anchors the top-list against a familiar phosphoric-acid/basic-polymer proton-conduction platform with strong acid retention, allowing the experimental team to compare whether the proposed biopolymer/clay anti-freeze designs truly add cold-side value. Including one exact-match-style benchmark is useful for sanity-checking conductivity trends and acid-retention measurements.
